rendering_findings.excerpt: 57: [L3] The bounded operators on a Banach space form a Banach space under the operator norm ([[thm-bounded-operator-space-is-banach]]). Composition is submultiplicative: $\|STb\|\le\|S\|\|T\|\|b\|$ for each $b$, and taking the unit-ball supremum gives $\|ST\|\le\|S\|\|T\|$. The required normalization for a nonzero unital Banach algebra is $\|1\|=1$ ([[def-unital-banach-algebra]]).

diagram_candidates.claim: For T=diag(1,2), the contour gamma(t)=1+(1/2)e^{it} separates spectral point 1 from 2 and its resolvent contour integral gives P_E=diag(1,0), with range Ce_1 and kernel Ce_2.
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: A compact figure can make the contour separation and resulting spectral summands immediately visible, while the local source gives exact coordinates, contour, map and output projection.
diagram_candidates.draw_or_check: Complex plane with points 1 and 2, positively oriented radius-1/2 circle around 1; alongside C^2 coordinate arrows e1↦1·e1 and e2↦2·e2, and projection P_E(e1)=e1, P_E(e2)=0. Mark range Ce1 and kernel Ce2. Preserve orientation and the circle’s exclusion of 2.
diagram_candidates.confidence: source-supported; usefulness is editorial judgment, not a confirmed missing requirement

diagram_candidates.claim: A bounded left inverse S satisfies ST=I_X; then P=TS is a bounded projection onto ran(T). Conversely, a bounded projection P:Y→ran(T) and R=T^{-1}:ran(T)→X give S=R∘P.
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The equivalence is explicitly a map-factorization statement across X, ran(T), and Y; one commuting/factorization diagram can clarify which composites are identities/projections.
diagram_candidates.draw_or_check: Show X --T--> ran(T) ↪ Y, R:ran(T)→X with RT=I_X on the range; in the forward direction show P=TS:Y→ran(T) and P^2=P; in the reverse direction show S=R∘P and ST=I_X. Do not imply T is onto Y.
diagram_candidates.confidence: source-supported; figure remains optional because the proof states the identities directly
